editorial:
Imagine waking up to find out your boss hates you and wants you gone. That is exactly what happens to fifty workers at Taiyo Real Estate. The big bad boss, Yokoyama, shoves them into a fake division and tells them to sell 1.5 billion yen worth of property in three months or they are fired. It feels like a total setup, and the vibe is a mix of stress and dark humor. You will really root for Shinoda and Takigawa, two guys who refuse to just take this lying down. They turn their anger into a mission to beat the system and save their coworkers' jobs.

What makes this work is seeing the underdog fight back against a greedy corporate jerk. The pacing is snappy, and the acting makes you feel the pressure of the ticking clock. While some of the business talk can be a bit dry, the satisfaction of seeing the bad guy sweat is worth it. If you enjoy stories about sticking it to the man, you should definitely give this a go. Try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a fan of old-school Japanese dramas, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move.
endingExplained: In the end, Shinoda and Takigawa use their smarts to beat the impossible goal. They manage to land a massive deal that puts Yokoyama in a tough spot. Instead of getting fired, the workers prove their worth and expose the boss's cruelty. Yokoyama loses his power and his pride as the company realizes the workers were the ones actually bringing in the money. It ends with a victory for the little guys and a big lesson in humility for the boss.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about working-class heroes beating a greedy boss.
